citeAs: Tjong Kim Sang, E.F. and De Meulder, F. (2003). Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003.
creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang, Fien De Meulder (CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp)
description: The CoNLL-2003 shared task dataset for language-independent named entity recognition, covering English and German. It contains annotated training, development, and test sets with four named entity types (persons, locations, organizations, and miscellaneous), plus large unannotated data files. English data is sourced from Reuters news stories; German data from the Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper.
name: CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition Dataset
publisher: CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotation was done at the University of Antwerp; no further demographic details provided.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Manual annotation performed at the University of Antwerp (no specific software platform named)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly MUC conventions were followed (Chinchor et al., 1999). An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names not in the other categories (persons, locations, organizations). The IOB tagging scheme (Ramshaw and Marcus, 1995) was used. Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping; when a named entity is embedded in another, usually only the top-level entity is annotated.
rai:dataCollection: English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus, consisting of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. Training and development sets used ten days of data from end of August 1996; test set used texts from December 1996. German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau. All three German splits were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. Unannotated data contain 17 million tokens (English) and 14 million tokens (German).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: English: Reuters Corpus (Reuters news stories, August 1996–August 1997). German: ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically the Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper (articles from August 1992; raw data from September–December 1992).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English data: August 1996 to December 1996 (training/dev from end of August 1996; test from December 1996; raw unannotated data from September 1996). German data: end of August 1992 (training/dev/test); raw unannotated data from September to December 1992.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and chunker were applied to the raw data. Two basic language-specific tokenizers were created. English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger (Daelemans et al., 2002). German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger (Schmid, 1995).
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset supports development of named entity recognition systems, which are important components of information extraction systems. It enables language-independent NER research across English and German.
rai:dataUseCases: Named entity recognition (NER) for English and German; benchmarking and evaluation of machine learning systems for information extraction; development of language-independent NER systems.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MBT (Memory-Based Tagger, Daelemans et al., 2002) used for POS tagging and chunking of English data; Treetagger (Schmid, 1995) used for lemmatization, POS tagging and chunking of German data.
